topic: What would happen if 1 US dollar were equal to 1 rupee?
angle: Why exchange rates aren't a scorecard; what a 1:1 rate would do to exports, imports, jobs, remittances, fuel prices and savings; how RBI manages the rupee; purchasing power parity vs market rate; examples of countries with strong/weak currencies and what that does and doesn't mean.

topic: Who is Rahul Gandhi? Education, career and the 'Pappu' label explained
angle: Factual biography (family, education with verified degrees and institutions, career, offices held, Bharat Jodo Yatra, Leader of Opposition from 2024). How the 'Pappu' nickname spread online, what fact-checkers (Alt News, BOOM, AFP etc.) found about edited or false clips and claims attributed to him, and what research/reporting says about organised social-media campaigns in Indian politics. Present what critics say too (gaffes, election results) and how public perception has changed. Don't name any party as the source of a campaign; say 'a political party's social media cell' or 'organised online campaigns' and stick to what sources document.

topic: What is per capita income? India's reality and the K-shaped economy
angle: Definition and how it's measured (GDP vs GNI per capita, nominal vs PPP); India's latest figures from MoSPI/World Bank/IMF and world rank; why a growing GDP and a low per capita income coexist; inequality data (World Inequality Lab, PLFS wages, consumption survey); what a K-shaped recovery/economy means with Indian examples (premium vs entry-level sales, wages); what the government and critics each say.

topic: What is a dictatorship and how did Hitler come to power?
angle: Definition and types of dictatorship vs democracy; the step-by-step history of how Hitler rose legally then dismantled democracy (1933 appointment, Reichstag fire decree, Enabling Act, banning parties and unions, Gleichschaltung, control of press and propaganda, 1934 merger of offices); warning signs political scientists describe (Levitsky & Ziblatt etc.) stated generally. Historical and general only; no comparisons to any current Indian leader or party.

topic: Is controlling the news media a sign of dictatorship?
angle: How authoritarian regimes have controlled media (censorship, ownership, licences, ads, intimidation); difference between regulation and control; what India's Constitution (Art. 19(1)(a), 19(2)) and Supreme Court say on press freedom; press freedom indices (RSF, Freedom House) with India's latest ranks and the government's stated objections to them; how readers can spot captured media. General and factual; name no party.

topic: Does a leader who gives no press conferences avoid accountability?
angle: Opinion piece (label it as opinion in the first lines). Argue that open press conferences are an important accountability tool: unscripted questions, follow-ups, a record. Use facts: how often leaders of democracies (US, UK, France, Japan etc.) hold them, past Indian PMs' practice, what reporting says about recent practice in India, stated factually without naming a party. Then fairly give the counter-arguments (Parliament, interviews, rallies, social media, RTI, elections as accountability) and answer them.

topic: What does the RTI Act give you? How to file an RTI application online and what to do if you get no reply
angle: What the Right to Information Act 2005 lets any citizen ask for; who must answer (public authorities, PIOs) and who is exempt (Section 24 organisations, with the corruption/human-rights exception); step-by-step filing on rtionline.gov.in for central bodies and state portals, the ₹10 fee and BPL exemption; time limits (30 days, 48 hours for life and liberty); first appeal and second appeal to the CIC/SIC; Section 8 exemptions; the 2019 amendment on information commissioners' tenure and pay and the 2023 DPDP Act change to Section 8(1)(j), each with the government's stated reason and critics' view in a sentence; CIC annual report figures on applications and pendency. Name no political party.

topic: How is inflation measured in India? CPI and WPI explained with the new base year
angle: What CPI and WPI measure, who publishes them (MoSPI/NSO and the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT), the basket and weights (food share), rural/urban/combined, the base-year revision, core vs headline inflation, why RBI targets CPI 4% ± 2% under the flexible inflation targeting framework, how to read a monthly release with a worked example, and why your own inflation can differ from the official one. Official figures only.

topic: What does the Election Commission of India do? Powers and limits explained
angle: Article 324, how commissioners are appointed (the 2023 Act and the earlier Supreme Court judgment, with the government's reasoning and critics' view in a sentence each), the Model Code of Conduct and its legal status, EVMs/VVPAT and what courts have ruled, electoral rolls and SIR/summary revision, what the ECI cannot do. No party named; no officeholder criticised or praised by name.

topic: How do the Centre and states share money? The Finance Commission explained
angle: Article 280, vertical devolution (states' share of the divisible pool) and horizontal formula (population, area, income distance, forest, demographic performance), cesses and surcharges outside the pool, GST compensation, the latest Finance Commission's award with official figures, why some states say they get back less than they contribute and the counter-argument, with a table of criteria and weights.

topic: What is GDP and how does India calculate it?
angle: GDP vs GVA, production/expenditure/income approaches, who publishes India's estimates (NSO/MoSPI), advance, provisional and revised estimates and why numbers change, quarterly GDP, the base-year revision, nominal vs real with a worked example, and the main debates about measurement (informal sector, deflators) with official responses. Official data only.

topic: Fundamental Rights vs Directive Principles: what's the difference?
angle: Part III vs Part IV of the Constitution, justiciable vs non-justiciable, the six Fundamental Rights groups with articles, key Directive Principles, landmark judgments (Champakam Dorairajan, Golaknath, Kesavananda Bharati, Minerva Mills) on the conflict, Fundamental Duties, a comparison table, and how DPSPs shaped real laws (MGNREGA, RTE, food security). No party named.

topic: How does a bill become a law in India?
angle: Stages in Parliament: introduction, first/second/third readings, standing committees, the other House, joint sittings (Article 108), the President's assent and options (Article 111), ordinary vs money bills (Articles 109-110) vs constitution amendment bills (Article 368), state bills and the Governor (Article 200, the 2023 and 2025 Supreme Court rulings on timelines, described accurately), with a flow table. Official sources (Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha rules, PRS). No party named.

topic: What is the repo rate and how does RBI's Monetary Policy Committee decide it?
angle: Repo, reverse repo, SDF and MSF in plain words; the MPC's six members and voting; the 4% (+/-2%) inflation target and who sets it; how a repo change reaches home-loan EMIs (EBLR) with a worked example; the latest policy decision with date and figure from RBI's statement; common myths. Official RBI data only. No party or officeholder praised or criticised.

topic: What is fiscal deficit and why does the Budget target it?
angle: Fiscal, revenue and primary deficit with a simple worked example; how the government borrows (G-secs, small savings); the FRBM Act and the shift to a debt-to-GDP anchor; latest Union Budget figures from the Budget at a Glance; why ratings agencies and economists watch it; states' deficits and borrowing limits; counter-views on deficit spending. Official data only. No party named.

topic: How is GST money shared between the Centre and the states?
angle: CGST, SGST and IGST and how IGST is settled; the GST Council's composition and voting (Article 279A); compensation cess and how it ended; devolution of the Centre's share via the Finance Commission; latest collection data from official releases; the main disputes states have raised and the Centre's response, described neutrally. No party named.

topic: What is a PIL and how do you file one?
angle: Public interest litigation: origin in the late 1970s-80s, landmark cases (Hussainara Khatoon, S.P. Gupta, M.C. Mehta, Vishaka), who can file and in which court (Article 32 vs 226), letter petitions, the steps and court fees as stated by the Supreme Court/High Courts, what courts reject (frivolous PILs, costs imposed), and alternatives such as RTI and grievance portals. No party named.

topic: Lok Sabha vs Rajya Sabha: how members are chosen and who has more power
angle: Direct vs indirect election, seats by state, terms, the Speaker vs Chairman, money bills, no-confidence motions, joint sittings, nominated members, the 2008 delimitation freeze and the debate on future delimitation (both views, neutrally), with a comparison table. Official sources (Constitution, Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha websites). No party named.
